title: Iterative Gaussian process screening discovers selective aurein-derived antifungal peptides
summary: An uncertainty-aware Gaussian process regression workflow iteratively selected 23 synthetic α/β-peptide analogues for synthesis and measurements of fungal inhibition and human-red-blood-cell hemolysis. One lead, peptide 6-4, was a measured variant of an existing aurein-derived template and achieved a selectivity index of 57.1 (60.9 using the study’s finer MIC interval) versus 1.2 for aurein 1.2. Its high selectivity was driven by low hemolysis; the result is a specific peptide-design and assay contribution, not a new peptide scaffold or evidence of therapeutic efficacy. The ChemRxiv v1 result was posted on 2024-10-04; the peer-reviewed journal article followed in 2025.
ai_technology: Iterative uncertainty-aware Gaussian process regression using molecular descriptors and measured antifungal/hemolysis labels

evidence.tested: Across six iterative rounds, uncertainty-aware Gaussian process regression selected 23 peptide variants for synthesis and antifungal/hemolysis assays. Lead 6-4 had a selectivity index of 57.1 (60.9 using the study’s finer MIC interval), versus 1.2 for aurein 1.2; the authors attribute the selectivity to reduced hemolysis.
evidence.unknown: Peptide 6-4 modifies a known aurein-derived template. The result is a measured sequence and assay outcome, not evidence of a new scaffold or therapeutic efficacy. The version-specific first public result is the 2024 ChemRxiv preprint; the journal article followed in 2025.
evidence.ai_role: An uncertainty-aware Gaussian process regression model selected peptide variants for synthesis and assays, and measured outcomes were fed back into subsequent selection rounds.

source_review.scope: Primary ChemRxiv version-history record and v2 manuscript; primary RSC indexed full article PDF, including sequence tables, Results, Methods and publication metadata; PubMed primary abstract/affiliation metadata.
